subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` adopt a hard 1 MiB maximum, or should it bound memory use while preserving the existing large-file CLI contract?
rationale: The size threshold is a new user-visible compatibility policy, not a mechanically determined bug fix, and no provided discussion records owner approval for its value or fallback behavior.

options.title: Preserve large-file compatibility
options.body: Use bounded or streaming file handling that prevents unbounded buffering without rejecting previously accepted regular files.

options.title: Adopt the 1 MiB contract
options.body: Approve the fixed limit explicitly and require upgrade-facing documentation and real proof of the expected rejection behavior.

recommendation.title: Preserve large-file compatibility
recommendation.body: Use bounded or streaming file handling that prevents unbounded buffering without rejecting previously accepted regular files.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR timeline shows direct review-routing involvement; stronger ownership attribution could not be established from the available read-only inspection.
